summary: Token-prefetch amplification triggering runtime watchdog resets and elevated 5xx rates
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC, Currentext Analytics (dedicated tenant in us-west) has reported a burst of 5xx errors on streaming and short-text endpoints. Pattern: elevated 502/503s correlated with increased token-prefetch activity from the serving runtime, followed by runtime watchdog restarts and GPU process resets.

Impact: ~18% error rate for requests from the tenant across multiple routes; degraded end-user experience for production customers; several long-lived streaming sessions dropped. Customer SLA at risk.

Environment: prod dedicated pool (us-west), pinned model gpt-3.5-xl-open v2026-02-10, autoscaler policy conservative-warmup-3, runtime version v1.18.4.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Synthetic load: many short-chat requests with high prefix overlap (repeated system messages + user templates) from the tenant.
2. Runtime prefetch triggers KV-prefetch path to warm caches.
3. Backend begins long-running prefetch CPU+GPU activity, connection queuing increases at api-gateway layer.
4. Watchdog notices stalled inference workers and triggers process-level restart, causing 502/503 responses upstream.

Observed behavior: 1) api-gateway 502 spikes in graphs at 03:10–03:40 UTC. 2) Serving runtime shows repeated watchdog SIGTERM->restart cycles with GPU reset messages. 3) Autoscaler did not immediately provision new nodes due to conservative warmup settings resulting in capacity shortfall. 4) KV cache thrash logged with high prefetch eviction rates.

Expected behavior: runtime should limit prefetch concurrency under high-queue conditions, autoscaler should provision burst capacity before watchdog escalates, API should degrade gracefully (429 backpressure) rather than return 5xx during transient overloads.

Initial hypothesis: token-prefetch path multiplies requests for shared prefixes (amplification) causing long-tail GPU occupancy; combined with conservative autoscaler settings results in watchdog-triggered restarts. Prefetch code path lacks a circuit-breaker for global concurrent prefetches per-tenant.

Attachments/links: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/tenant/Currentext/overview?panel=5, logs: https://logs.redwood/query?q=tenant%3ACurrentext+watchdog+reset, slack thread: #support-currentext (thread ts 1643421).
investigation_notes:
2026-03-12 04:00 UTC - Support intake: customer provided replay traces and Jaeger spans.
2026-03-12 04:30 UTC - SRE captured runtime logs: repeated 'watchdog: worker unresponsive after 45s' and 'gpu: resetting process'.
2026-03-12 05:10 UTC - Correlated peaks: prefetch-rps increased 6x for tenant during burst window.
2026-03-12 06:00 UTC - Heap and GPU memory within nominal range; CPU saturation on prefetch threads and kernel queue growth observed.
2026-03-12 07:20 UTC - Autoscaler events show scale-up attempts delayed by warmup gating policy; new nodes come online ~90s after first watchdog restart.
2026-03-12 08:00 UTC - SRE reproduced amplification locally by simulating concurrent requests with identical prefixes; confirmed prefetch fanout produces N prefetched KV ops per request where N scales with unique prefixes in the batch.
Hypotheses refined: prefetch concurrency combined with KV cache eviction leads to thrash and long-lived GPU tasks. Watchdog threshold too aggressive for this workload shape.
Follow-ups planned: add tenant-level prefetch concurrency cap, instrument prefetch request counters in runtime metrics, adjust autoscaler warmup thresholds for dedicated pools, consider temporary increase of watchdog timeout for affected pool.
comments: 2026-03-12 04:05 - Support (Daniel Park): Opened intake ticket after receiving error traces from Currentext. Noted immediate customer impact and requested priority escalation.
2026-03-12 04:45 - SRE (Linnea Gómez): Attached runtime logs showing watchdog restarts. Kicked off local reproduction. Marking incident Sev1 and notifying on-call kernel team.
2026-03-12 06:30 - Customer (Maya Singh, Currentext): Confirmed degraded UX. Provided sample request IDs and said they saw spike after nightly data sync at 03:00 UTC.

2026-03-12 07:45 - SRE (Linnea Gómez): Reproduction steps posted to the ticket. Implemented a temporary routing rule to divert 20% of Currentext traffic to a warmed burst pool as mitigation. Monitoring error rate.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Support (Daniel Park): Customer confirmed error rate reduced to ~3% after diversion. They requested permanent mitigation plan and root cause details.
2026-03-13 11:20 - Engineering (Rahul Mehta): Proposed code change: add global_prefetch_limit and a prefetch backoff when queue depth crosses threshold. Draft PR incoming.

2026-03-14 10:00 - SRE (Linnea Gómez): Temporary autoscaler policy tweak applied for Currentext dedicated pool to lower warmup gating. Observed stable behavior for 24h. Planning rollback to default after code fix is deployed.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: 2026-03-12 07:50 UTC routed 20% of tenant traffic to warmed burst pool; 2026-03-12 09:00 autoscaler gating temporarily relaxed for the dedicated pool.
Permanent fix: engineering to land PR that introduces tenant-level prefetch concurrency cap and prefetch backoff (PR referenced above). Also increasing watchdog threshold for prefetch-heavy workloads pending deployment.
Customer impact: Error rate reduced from ~18% to ~3% post-mitigation. No data loss.
Next steps: schedule patch release in stable channel (target 2026-03-20), add synthetic alerts to detect prefetch amplification early, and run a postmortem documenting prevention actions.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to finalize PR and run canary (owner: Rahul Mehta, ETA 2026-03-18). 2) SRE to keep autoscaler gating relaxed for Currentext until patch is rolled out (owner: Linnea Gómez). 3) Support to coordinate customer communication and postmortem (owner: Daniel Park). 4) Create alert rule for 'prefetch_rps_per_tenant > 5x baseline' and 'watchdog_restart_rate > 0.5/min' (owner: Observability team).
time_to_restore: ~2 hours to partial mitigation, ~26 hours to stable with autoscaler tweak
public_status_page_note: Investigating elevated 5xx rates affecting a single dedicated tenant in us-west; mitigation in place. Customers on Dedicated may see transient errors. More updates to follow.
